steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine sugar, melted butter, and vanilla in a large bowl. Beat in eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition, until thoroughly blended.
Sift flour, cocoa powder, and salt into a separate large bowl. Gradually stir flour mixture into egg mixture until blended; stir in chocolate chips.
Spread batter evenly into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is dry and edges have started to pull away from the sides of the pan, about 35 to 40 minutes.
Let cool completely before slicing into 24 squares.

review.reviewBody: These brownies came out great, so fudgy and chewy! Sine there is extra egg in place of the usual oil and no baking soda/powder, the result is an intensely rich, decadent brownie. I used milk chocolate chips and used 1 1/2 c. white sugar and 1 1/2 c. brown sugar. I have found that this adds a more saturated, special flavor. The best way I have found to melt sticks of butter is to place them in a large, microwaveable Tupperware cup and microwave them for 30+ seconds. By doing this, you don't have to go through the hastle of cutting the butter. Also, in place of sifting the flour mixture, all you need to do is whisk it. Whisking produces the exact same effect/texture as using a conventional sifter, plus it is much easier to clean! I highly reccomend this recipe. You have got a winner with this one Brooke!

Delicious! These are dense and rich! If you don't like a sweet, fudgy brownie, don't make these. Most of the lower ratings were due to people decreasing the amount of sugar. If you want a 5 star brownie, use all 3c. of sugar. If you want a 3 star recipe, decrease your sugar...its that simple.

I loved the taste of this brownie and the texture. Seriously perfect perfect fudgey brownies. This is MUCH BETTER overnight as the butter doesn't ooze and the sugar taste becomes more neutral. This is a lot of sugar for my taste so I cut it down to 2 cups and even then it was sweet. Something I learned from a chef I knew: Beat your eggs till they go a light yellow then gradually add the sugar. Mix your cocoa and butter or dark chocolate (with a v high cocoa %) in a microwave or over the stove. Let it cool then fold into the fluffy egg mix and then slowly fold in the flour. For some reason this always ensures I have fudgey brownies and never dry ones.

I made this in a 13 × 9 in pan. I made everything according to recipe, except: I added 1/4 tsp baking soda for the crackly top, 1/4 tsp garam masala, and some pecans. I forgot to fold in the chocolate chips and pecans, so halfway through the brownies, i put a layer of pecans, and put 1/2 the chocolate chips on top of them (so they wouldn't sink to the bottom). Mixed the last half with the remaining batter and smoothed on top of the pecans/chocolate chips. I sprinkled a tiny bit of chili powder on them at the end to give more of a warming effect. Brownies were thick, and as gooey as skillet brownies, and the top was super crackly and crispy (baking soda). This recipe makes a ton of brownies, but it is worth it. Boyfriend doesn't want to share them with his coworkers. 
You won't regret making these!

Unbelievably delicious brownies!!! I used 1/2 brown sugar and 1/2 white sugar to total the 3 cups. I also used 1/2 c. white chocolate chips and 1/2 c. semisweet chocolate chips. I also added 1/2 c. finely chopped walnuts and 2 Tbsp freshly brewed coffee, then sprinkled them lightly before baking with kosher salt (to combat all the sweetness). These are fantastic—so fudgy and perfect texture! After reading another review about “weird” texture, I melted the sugar with the butter and mixed in vanilla extract and coffee before mixing in additional ingredients. These are a must!!! Go make them!!

I used 2 separate bowls, one for dry and the other for wet ingredients. I added my dry ingredients to the wet mixture (usually I do the opposite) but it makes it easier to incorporate without over mixing. Instead of creaming my eggs and sugar with a hand mixer, I just used a tablespoon. Used a tablespoon throughout, I reduced the sugar slightly to 2 1/2 cups and baked for 28 minutes at 350 degrees...perfection.

These are definitely the best brownies yet. My changes: used 1 cup brown sugar and 1 1/2 cups white sugar, added 1/2 tsp baking soda for a nice top crust, and I found that 30 minutes at 350 was perfect to produce a fudgy brownie without any gooey-ness. Next time will add some walnuts or pecans.

I have made this recipe multiple times and it is one of the best out there. There are a couple of tweaks that I have done to make them stand out a little more. The quality of the ingredients is important so I use Dutch cocoa and Belgium chocolate chips. In addition, I add approx. 1 Tbsp of instant espresso powder and put flaky salt on top. You can also brown the butter, which will give it a nutty flavor without having to add nuts, although you can most certainly do that as well. Great recipe!
Great recipe! I used half white sugar and half brown sugar and cut the cocoa powder down to 3/4 of a cup. I found baking them at 325 for 50 minutes made a chewier, less cakey brownie.

when made right they are fudgy and moist and we can eat them from three days!!! i dont remember using 4 eggs i have been using this recipe for over three years. i use 3 eggs substitute sugar for half brown half white any kind(stevia, or truvia) i use erythritol. i have to bake for less time because i have a convection oven so i bake for 25min instead 30-35. wish i took a picture.
Excellent! I added 1/4 tsp baking powder, in case they would be too dense, cut the recipe in half and baked them 25 min in a9" x 9" pan. They're great!

All of my family loved it I made 1/2 the recipe and it made 9 brownies. Make sure to cook it almost all the way through then take it out so you don't make it too crispy. Would definitely recommend this recipe.

I followed the recipe exactly and ate them a couple of hours after making, and they were AMAZING. My family could not stop raving about how delicious they were and I even loved them--and brownies are not my thing. So good and easy to make. I did have to tweak the time a bit, but if you keep your eyes on the pan it's easy to get it right.
Granddaughter, waiting for the brownie's to cool, says I'm the best grandma in the world! Made it as is and they are so good!
Best brownies I ever made or ate. No more box mix for me!
I made this exactly as the recipe stated; brought it to a potluck and people couldn't stop talking about how good these were.

Made these for my daughter and grandchildren this afternoon. They were a hit. I added walnuts. I thought they were a little too gooey but no one else seemed to think so. I baked it for 45 minutes. That added a thin crispy top crust that everyone liked.
It was very good, only took me 10 minutes to make. The pan was empty the same day. Definitely something I will make again.

These are soooo good! I like fudgie gooey brownies and these are it. My family loves them and I get many compliments when I take them to events. Oh…and I thought they would have had a lot more calories. They are only 248 each. Can I cheat and eat a second one? 😉
I added chopped Pecans in the recipe.
